articles.title: Weather & Floods: Rising Ganga Water Disrupts Ganga Aarti in Varanasi, Monsoon Fury Hits Himachal and Bihar
articles.description: The rising water level of the Ganga in Varanasi is beginning to affect the city’s iconic Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat. As the river continues to rise, the designated location for the evening aarti has been shifted around 15 feet backward from its usual position. Several parts of the ghats are already submerged, but the growing water level has not reduced the enthusiasm of devotees, who continue to gather in large numbers. Authorities may have to shift the aarti further if the river continues to rise. Meanwhile, heavy monsoon rains have triggered landslides and road disruptions across Himachal Pradesh. In Chamba’s Khuni Nala area, debris and rocks fell onto the National Highway, creating a serious threat to motorists. According to the state disaster management authorities, between June 30 and August 7, rain-related incidents have reportedly claimed 150 lives, injured 226 people and left two people missing. Kangra, Chamba, Shimla and Mandi are among the worst-affected districts. In Bihar, heavy rainfall in Nepal is affecting border districts. Flooding in East Champaran has damaged embankments and submerged villages and thousands of acres of crops. More than 24 villages are reportedly affected. In West Champaran, the rising Gandak River has flooded low-lying areas and roads. SSB personnel are assisting residents stranded in floodwaters and helping them reach safer areas.

articles.title: WATCH: Uttarakhand Innovator’s Electric Flying Vehicle Takes Maiden Test Flight
articles.description: Ravi Tamta from Kaflikhan village in Almora, Uttarakhand, has test-flown a single-seater electric flying vehicle prototype developed under his startup, Hapida Sky. Named HAPIDA SKYNeX, the machine is claimed to be based on modified drone technology. Videos of its initial flight have drawn attention on social media, with Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami also sharing the video on X. Tamta says the idea was inspired by travel difficulties in the hills, where a roughly 40-kilometre road journey can take nearly 90 minutes. He envisions covering the same distance in 10 to 15 minutes using the vehicle. The prototype was tested on open ground in Almora. Tamta has denied claims that it was imported from China. Technical details such as battery capacity, speed and flight duration remain undisclosed.
